issues.legal_issue: An ex parte eviction decree should be set aside where minor defendants with a substantial tenancy interest were ineffectively represented and the service of process was inefficient.
material_facts: The deceased tenant left a widow and three minor children who had lived with him at the time of his death, giving the children a substantial interest in the tenancy under the governing rent law.
The summons and amended summons were returned marked “left,” and service was then attempted by affixing them to the premises.
The court appointed its Registrar as guardian for the minors; the minors did not receive effective assistance or meaningful participation in the proceedings before the ex parte decree was made.
The suit sought arrears of rent and possession, and the decree was affirmed by the superior courts before the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the ex parte decree was set aside, and the suit was remitted to the trial court for adjudication from the stage at which proceedings had gone ex parte against the appellants.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(11)(c)(i) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 provides for tenancy to pass on a tenant’s death to a qualifying family member residing with the tenant, or, in the absence of such a member, to an heir as determined by the court. Where that transmission gives minors a substantial stake in a suit, the court, as guardian of minors, must seek their effective participation. Procedural lapses warrant indulgent consideration when minors are represented only by an official guardian without an interest in the proceedings and service is inefficient, even if formally attempted. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_ex_parte_decree: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decree made in the defendants’ absence.
predicates.minor_defendants_have_substantial_legal_: Minor defendants have a substantial legal interest in the subject matter of the suit.
predicates.official_guardian_lacks_interest_and_eff: The minors are represented by a person appointed by virtue of office who lacks an interest in the case and does not provide effective assistance.
predicates.service_is_inefficient: The process was formally attempted but did not effectively bring the proceedings to the defendants’ attention.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an ex parte decree, minor defendants have a substantial legal interest, their official guardian lacks interest and effective assistance, and service is inefficient, the decree is set aside and the case is remanded.
